_patient.input_block:
63M, ELECTIVE admission from PHYSICIAN REFERRAL.
OUTCOME: discharged alive to HOME
PRESENTING SYMPTOMS: Nausea alone; Chills (without fever); Other malaise and fatigue
PRIMARY DIAGNOSIS: Encounter for antineoplastic immunotherapy
ACTIVE DIAGNOSES: Toxic encephalopathy; Malignant neoplasm of kidney, except pelvis; Secondary malignant neoplasm of lung; Drug induced neutropenia; Dermatitis due to drugs and medicines taken internally; Antineoplastic chemotherapy induced anemia; Disorders of magnesium metabolism; Other secondary thrombocytopenia; Unspecified pruritic disorder
PAST MEDICAL HISTORY: Encounter for antineoplastic immunotherapy; Personal history of malignant neoplasm of prostate; Personal history of irradiation, presenting hazards to health
PROCEDURES: Venous catheterization, not elsewhere classified; High-dose infusion interleukin-2 [IL-2]; Central venous catheter placement with guidance
MEDICATIONS: Prochlorperazine 10mg PO; 0.9% Sodium Chloride 250mL IV; Calcium Gluconate 4g IV; Diphenoxylate-Atropine 1-2TAB PO; Naproxen 375mg PO; Bag 100mL IV; Magnesium Sulfate 4gm IV; Levothyroxine Sodium 25mcg PO/NG; Acetaminophen 975mg PO; Heparin Flush (10 units/ml) 1mL IV; Lorazepam 1mg IV; SW 200mL IV; Potassium Chloride 20mEq IV; Ondansetron 8mg IV; 5% Dextrose 250mL IV DRIP; PHENYLEPHrine 60mg IV DRIP; Sodium Chloride 0.9%  Flush 3mL IV; DiphenhydrAMINE 25-50mg PO; Artificial Tears 1-2DROP BOTH EYES; Cephalexin 500mg PO; Ranitidine 150mg PO; D5W 250mL IV DRIP; DOPamine 400mg IV DRIP; Hydrocerin 1Appl TP; Maalox/Diphenhydramine/Lidocaine 5mL PO; Phosphorus 500mg PO; Sodium Acetate 100mEq IV; Aldesleukin 56.6Million Units IV; Meperidine 25-50mg IV; Sarna Lotion 1Appl TP
MICROBIOLOGY: none
SERVICES: OMED
WARDS: Hematology/Oncology
_patient.note:
[1] The patient is a 63-year-old male admitted electively from physician referral.
[2] The patient presented with nausea, chills without fever, and malaise.
[3] The primary diagnosis is encounter for antineoplastic immunotherapy.
[4] Active diagnoses include toxic encephalopathy, malignant neoplasm of kidney, except pelvis, secondary malignant neoplasm of lung, drug induced neutropenia, dermatitis due to drugs and medicines taken internally, antineoplastic chemotherapy induced anemia, disorders of magnesium metabolism, other secondary thrombocytopenia, and unspecified pruritic disorder.
[5] Past medical history includes encounter for antineoplastic immunotherapy and personal history of malignant neoplasm of prostate and irradiation presenting hazards to health.
[6] Procedures performed include venous catheterization, high-dose infusion interleukin-2 [IL-2], and central venous catheter placement with guidance.
[7] Medications administered include prochlorperazine, 0.9% Sodium Chloride, Calcium Gluconate, Diphenoxylate-Atropine, Naproxen, Bag, Magnesium Sulfate, Levothyroxine Sodium, Acetaminophen, Heparin Flush, Lorazepam, SW, Potassium Chloride, Ondansetron, 5% Dextrose, PHENYLEPHrine, Sodium Chloride Flush, DiphenhydrAMINE, Artificial Tears, Cephalexin, Ranitidine, D5W, DOPamine, Hydrocerin, Maalox/Diphenhydramine/Lidocaine, Phosphorus, Sodium Acetate, Aldesleukin, Meperidine, and Sarna Lotion.
[8] Microscopic analysis revealed no organisms.
[9] The patient was managed by the OMED service.
[10] The patient was admitted to the Hematology/Oncology ward.
[11] The patient was discharged alive to home.
